I will keep my land in the crop pattern I know best: winter wheat followed by summer maize. I am in Quzhou County, and this is still the main grain pattern here. Local material says Quzhou had about 473,000 mu of wheat in 2024, and research from the Quzhou experimental station says more than 80% of fields there are in a winter wheat and summer maize rotation. I will not switch into cotton or vegetables this year. They are workable in Quzhou too, but at 70 years old I want a system I can manage steadily with less labor risk, more machine work, and more certain grain output. I will stay with familiar improved wheat seed and hybrid maize seed, keep fertilizer at moderate local levels instead of pushing too hard, irrigate wheat more than maize because summer rain usually helps maize, and use simple pest control only when needed. I am also deciding this around the actual season: by mid-April 2026 my winter wheat is already in the field, and I am planning the maize that will follow after the June wheat harvest. Sources I used: [Hebei/Quzhou spring farming report](https://www.agri.cn/zx/xxlb/hb/202403/t20240305_8613211.htm), [Quzhou wheat-maize rotation background](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5290742/), [Quzhou “green ton-and-a-half grain” results](https://qzsyz.cau.edu.cn/art/2024/10/8/art_46317_1039835.html), [CAU Quzhou station on the local wheat-maize technology](https://qzsyz.cau.edu.cn/art/2024/2/25/art_46232_1012984.html), and [Hebei maize fertilization ranges](https://www.zynylm.com/zhibao/2019/0222/3071.html). My phosphorus and potassium figures are my own practical choice inferred from the local nitrogen rates and standard wheat-maize nutrient ratios.
